comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
LIVE DC-HARNESS FINDING (operator run 31807853902): test_live_rich_text_renders_and_echo_is_safe FAILED at the heading assertion — Jira rendered raw Markdown (# heading -> <ol>, **bold** -> literal *, fenced code -> literal backticks). Root-caused to TWO bugs in the TEST (not a 3388 production defect):

1) The test never enabled the DC rich-text cutover, so WikiTextCodec.to_wire was the IDENTITY. reconciler.rich_text_cutover ships 'off' (rich_text.py cutover_clients()), so WikiTextCodec(rich='dc' in cutover_clients()) is rich=False and sends Markdown verbatim. FIX: the rendered-HTML test now monkeypatch.setenv('REBAR_RECONCILER_RICH_TEXT_CUTOVER','dc') before pushing; run_bridge builds the subprocess env from os.environ via engine_env, so cutover_clients() in the child returns {'dc'} and to_wire renders Markdown->wiki (# x -> 'h1. x', **b** -> '*b*'). This is precisely the residual risk graywolf proves closed WHEN the cutover is on.

2) The code representative was a Markdown fenced block, which wiki_render LOCKS as _EXACT (code passes through byte-for-byte, never becomes {code}) — so it could never render a code macro. FIX: _rich_markdown now authors the code fragment as a literal Jira {code} macro (classified _EXACT by _WIKI_MACRO_RE, passed through unchanged for Jira to render as a <pre> code panel).

Verified in-process: to_wire('# h

**b**

{code}
c
{code}') -> 'h1. h

*b*

{code}
c
{code}'. Local gates green (make lint incl complexity ratchet, make typecheck, contract test 10 passed, live tests collect+skip cleanly). pandoc is present in the harness via the dev extra's pypandoc-binary==1.15 (the DC-harness job installs --extra dev --extra jira-datacenter). test_live_rich_text_both_sides_conflict_keeps_local is unchanged in behavior (it asserts token presence + local-wins + conflict alert, not rendering) and stays passing. Pushing a NEW Gerrit change (1766 already merged).

# Live DC harness (rendered HTML) + cross-repo contract test

## Context / Problem
The DC codec is validated offline against pandoc's jira reader as a proxy, but the
real Jira DC wiki renderer and Jira's own storage canonicalization differ from pandoc
and cannot be modeled offline — that gap is the residual risk this story closes. The
repo already runs live DC testing with a Dockerized Jira 8.17.1 instance in GitHub
Actions (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/`), so this extends that harness rather than
building a new one. Separately, the sibling repo `agentic-dev-platform` imports the
`InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text` seam from this package, so changing its behavior
must be guarded by a contract test.

This story is the LIVE proof of the state-based echo-safety and settled-conflict
behavior that `5c0e` (DC render robustness) and `3388` (cutover + echo suppression +
local-wins conflict) deliver; it depends on both.

## Approach
Extend the existing Docker DC harness with a rich-text test that:
- renders a representative body and pushes it via the real API
  (`rebar.edit_ticket(local_id, repo_root=repo, description=value)`, the pattern
  already used by `_out_description` in
  `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py`), and asserts **rendered HTML**
  through `?expand=renderedFields` — not just the wiki source via `?fields=description`
  — so we verify what Jira actually interprets (`*foo*`→bold, `h1.`→heading,
  `{code}`→macro). No `renderedFields`/`expand=` assertion exists in the harness
  today, so this is a genuinely new fidelity check.
- runs a second reconcile pass to assert **state-based echo-safety end-to-end** (the
  landed rich body decodes to a value the differ recognizes as unchanged → no
  re-push), exercising `3388`'s once-only-upgrade-then-converge path against the real
  renderer.
- performs a **both-sides concurrent edit** to assert `3388`'s settled conflict
  behavior with the precondition that policy actually requires. The
  `outbound-field-conflict` alert fires ONLY on a both-sides divergence
  (`local != baseline` AND `remote != baseline`, `outbound_field_diff.py:354-362`); a
  bare Jira-side edit with local unchanged is instead suppressed by the
  directionality guard (`_suppressed_by_inbound`) and mirrored inbound (Jira-wins)
  with NO conflict alert. So the live scenario is: (1) push a body and let a pass
  converge so a baseline is recorded; (2) make a **rebar-side** edit to the
  description AND a **Jira-side** edit to the same field before the next pass;
  (3) assert the next pass emits rebar's body (**local-wins**) and records the
  deduped `outbound-field-conflict:<key>:description` bridge alert — the remote value
  is recorded, never silently destroyed (NOT a novel LWW clock; this is the a713 +
  `3388` policy proven live, mirroring `3388`'s `test_concurrent_conflict_alerts`
  precondition).

Gate it with the harness's existing skip markers (absent-harness / absent-extra) and
the session-scoped PAT the harness already provisions. Add a contract test that pins
the public shape/behavior of `normalize_rich_text`
(`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py:134`, exposed as
`InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text`) so a change that would break the
`agentic-dev-platform` import fails here first.

## Scope
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` — new rich-text live test module (render+push,
  `?expand=renderedFields` HTML assertions, 2nd-pass echo, both-sides-concurrent-edit
  local-wins + conflict-alert assertion), reusing the existing conftest
  fixtures/skip markers.
- CI workflow for the DC harness job — ensure the new test runs in the existing
  amd64 Docker job (no new job).
- `tests/` — cross-repo `normalize_rich_text` contract test.

## Testing
- Live render fidelity: a pushed rich body's `renderedFields` HTML contains the
  expected bold/heading/code-macro markup (skipped when the harness/extra is absent).
- Live echo-safety: a second reconcile pass against the live instance pushes no
  description change (upgrade-then-converge holds against the real renderer).
- Live conflict: with a converged baseline, a **both-sides** edit (rebar-side AND
  Jira-side to the description) before the next pass keeps rebar's body and raises the
  deduped `outbound-field-conflict:<key>:description` alert (remote value recorded,
  not clobbered); a bare Jira-only edit is NOT asserted as a conflict (it is
  Jira-wins inbound).
- Contract: `normalize_rich_text` accepts the documented inputs and returns the
  documented type/shape; a signature/behavior change fails
  `test_normalize_rich_text_contract`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [operator-attested] [ ] The Docker DC harness has a rich-text test asserting rendered HTML via
  `?expand=renderedFields` (not just wiki source), covering bold/heading/code-macro;
  verified by the test running in the existing DC-harness CI job.
- [operator-attested] [ ] The live test asserts state-based echo-safety across a second pass (no re-push)
  AND `3388`'s settled local-wins + `outbound-field-conflict` bridge alert under the
  required **both-sides** precondition (converged baseline, then a rebar-side AND a
  Jira-side edit to the description → local-wins emit + deduped
  `outbound-field-conflict:<key>:description`, remote value recorded, not silently
  destroyed); verified by the same live test.
- [x] A cross-repo contract test pins `normalize_rich_text`
  (`InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text`) back-compat so a breaking change fails here
  first; verified by `test_normalize_rich_text_contract`.
